d: The square of a small town on the Tuscan coast. On the right, on three steps, an ancient façade of church with the bell tower on one side and on the other the house of the prevosto. To the left the cottage of the spice, with the door with two doors and on the side a window equipped with iron. In the middle of the square a fountain with a tub adorned with monsters. Night: a pale lunar dawn illuminates that little horizon that you see; the rest is in the deep darkness. Baldo looks out from the right, looking; in passing in front of the church you mark; traverses by wolf, waters by the window of the spice house. After a moment will appear behind the inferriata Candida.

A kind of strange dining room and a bit 'to receive and that serves also as a kitchen and pharmaceutical laboratory on the right side, where a wide and low arch shows the inside of the tiny shop of the spice. The octagonal room in a tower of Mr. Ipsilonne's castle. On the first side (left of the viewer) a door to the rooms of Candida, then a large sofa to the Turkish, a small table, two large deep armchairs and a very rich screen. On the second side, wide window opening onto a corner verone: the verone must also be accessed from the first room of the apartment of Candida. The verone is illuminated by torches; you can glimpse large hairs of trees and the sea far away. The third side is all glassed above large halls of light-lighting ballrooms. On the fourth side a magnificent fireplace with a golden pendulum, and in front of the fireplace other small table and other comfortable armchairs; on the table three bottles, one of which is already empty, and a huge piece of cake. A rich chandelier hangs from the ceiling: all in the room is rich, lavish, gold overload, with embellishments, embellishments of barments.

The square, as in the prologue. On the stairway of the church is laid a Vagabondo with a thick grey beard, wrapped in a great cloak and with a hood right on the eyes. At the end Candida and Baldo followed by two young Companions: Baldo beats at the door of the house of the front, until the window opens and faces, curled and sleepy, Menica.
